literal.prompt: Какой император подписал Манифест 17 октября 1905 года?

literalGroups.primaryGround: Все четыре ответа — императоры одной категории; сохранённый контекст Президентской библиотеки прямо связывает Николая II с Манифестом 17 октября 1905 года и его последствиями.

literalGroups.literal: Николай II подписал Манифест 17 октября 1905 года в ходе октябрьской политической стачки. Документ провозгласил гражданские свободы, а Государственная дума получила законодательные права.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The retained Presidential Library pages place the Manifesto in the October political strike, say Nicholas II signed it, report democratic/civic freedoms, and state that the Duma received legislative rights.

literalGroups.literal: Александр II провёл Великие реформы, включая отмену крепостного права.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The official Presidential Library account says Alexander II signed the 1861 emancipation manifesto and describes his reforms, including zemstvo, city, education, and judicial changes.

literalGroups.literal: Николай II подписал Манифест 17 октября 1905 года; документ провозгласил гражданские свободы, а Государственная дума получила законодательные права.
literalGroups.primaryGround: This correct-option note adds the concrete consequences of the decree beyond the signer asked for in the prompt: proclaimed civil freedoms and legislative rights for the Duma.

literalGroups.literal: Александр III умер в 1894 году; перед смертью он обязал сына подписать манифест о восшествии на престол.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The retained official page states Alexander III died in 1894 and, shortly before death, required his son to sign the accession manifesto; this identifies a separate, earlier reign from the 1905 signer.

literalGroups.literal: Николай I создал Третье отделение собственной канцелярии в 1826 году.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The Presidential Library page states that by decree of Nicholas I the Third Department was established on 15 July 1826 and that the Special Chancellery was transformed into an independent institution.

entries.correctNoteNewFact: Beyond asking which emperor signed the Manifesto, note1 names two concrete consequences: civil freedoms were proclaimed and the State Duma received legislative rights. Presidential Library locators turn2view0 L45 and turn5view0 L54.
entries.absoluteDifficulty: MEDIUM: a player familiar with Russian history is likely to connect the 1905 October Manifesto with Nicholas II; someone outside the topic mainly narrows the choices by historical period. The four answers are comparable imperial rulers, and no option is absurd. The date and decree require thematic knowledge rather than a multi-step inference.
